messages:
maria: heads up — saw a customer hit a bunch of 413s when they send mixed-dim arrays and our splitter goes wild. thinking we should expose a tiny preflight/shape signal so router can decide before doing destructive splits. thoughts?
kevin: do you mean an explicit preview endpoint or a lightweight header on the same call?
kevin: e.g. `X-Embed-Preview: 1` vs `X-Embed-Shape` inline header. leaning header so client flow stays 1x request.
olivia: prefer `X-Embed-Shape` with compact fields (count, dim, bytes). router uses it to pick route/quota and avoid unnecessary 413s.
sam: careful: bytes estimate is tricky with gzip and framing. we could require uncompressed bytes or let client provide `bytes=` as best-effort. router should fallback to `content-length` if missing.
kevin: sample header proposal:
```
X-Embed-Shape: count=6;dim=1536;bytes=98304
```
maria: exact — and server can return an advisory header with estimated processing units so clients know cost before splitting: `X-Embed-Budget: 9` meaning 9 batch-slots. this helps console cost previews.
olivia: telemetry-wise we should emit `embed.request.shape` metric (count, dim, bytes) + `embed.router.decision` tag (routed|split|reject). also `embed.split.count`. these will help tune routing thresholds.
will: how should we indicate reason when we reject? 413 vs 429 vs 409 debate. 413 is currently overloaded for both payload decoding and our split limit. i'd rather keep 413 for raw payload bytes and use 422 or 429 for routing quota decisions.
sam: +1 for distinct codes. customers get confused when content is valid but router refuses. 429 + `Retry-After` seems standard for soft-limits. also include `X-Embed-Decision: rejected` and `X-Embed-Explain: quota-exceeded-route:small-alloc` for human debuggability.
kevin: agree. summary: 413 = payload too big/invalid framing, 429 = router quota/slot unavailable, include `X-Embed-Decision` and `X-Embed-Budget`.
maria: console UX: add columns for `shape` and `est_units` in the request log and surface split occurrences as a warning icon with tooltip. also add a toggle to show raw `X-Embed-Shape` header.
olivia: rollout plan: feature-flag header support on router, canary route with `embed-shape-v3`, emit telemetry with `canary=true/false` tag. after 2 weeks of no regressions, flip default.
kevin: security note: we must not log raw embedding payloads. if we sample, limit to metadata (count/dim/bytes) and optionally first 32 bytes only when `X-Debug-Embed-Sample: 1` is present and tenant opts in. avoid storing vectors.
sam: add guard: `embed.sampled` metric and mask any sampled bytes in audit log. engineers: make it easy to opt-out in enterprise Private deployments.
infra-bot: deploy: started canary deploy `embed-router/embed-shape-v3` -> 10% traffic (eng-platform-canary)
maria: RFC next steps — i'll open a PR with header schema, router changes, and telemetry plan. will you folks review? @kevin @olivia @sam
kevin: will review tomorrow. please include fallback rule for pre-quantized dims and mixed-dim clients (we might map to a compat path).
olivia: i'll mock the console column and a small dashboard for `embed.router.decision` and send screenshots in the PR thread. :thumbsup:
will: 👍 and add a small runbook snippet for ops: how to interpret `X-Embed-Budget` and actions when 429 spikes.
maria: thanks — aiming to cut the PR by EOD and land canary next week.
